title: Hunza & Skardu Grand
summary: Nine days by road from Lahore up the Karakoram Highway: three nights in Hunza, then Skardu, its lakes and the Deosai plains.

image.alt: Turquoise Attabad Lake below a sunlit mountain, with boats and ferry pontoons at the jetty

overview.headline: Nine days up the Karakoram Highway to Hunza and Skardu
paragraphs: We drive up from Lahore on the motorway and the Karakoram Highway. Then we spend three nights in Hunza under Rakaposhi, and cross to Skardu for its lakes and the high Deosai plains.

This is a road trip at heart. The drive between stops is part of the trip: the Indus gorge, the place where three mountain ranges meet, the turquoise of Attabad. Your driver and guide set the pace, plan around the weather and know where to stop for chai.
suitedTo: First-time visitors who want Hunza and Skardu in one trip
Families with school-age children, and parents who like a planned pace
Couples and friends who would rather not drive the Karakoram Highway themselves
notSuitedTo: Travellers who dislike long road journeys. Days 2 and 9 are 11 hours or more
Anyone after a real trek (see the Fairy Meadows Trek)
Serious heart or breathing conditions at altitude. Check with your doctor first
Travellers who need luxury hotels every night; Chilas is simple

itinerary.title: Lahore → Islamabad
itinerary.text: Leave Lahore early and head north on the M-2 through the Salt Range. The evening in Islamabad is free.

itinerary.title: Islamabad → Chilas
itinerary.text: Onto the Karakoram Highway past Abbottabad and Besham, then along the Indus into the mountains. A long day, with plenty of stops for tea.

itinerary.title: Chilas → Hunza
itinerary.text: Stop at the Nanga Parbat viewpoint and the place where the Himalaya, Karakoram and Hindu Kush meet. Then on through Gilgit to Rakaposhi viewpoint and Karimabad.

itinerary.title: Hunza
itinerary.text: Baltit and Altit forts in the morning and Karimabad bazaar after lunch, then sunset from Eagle’s Nest above the valley.

itinerary.title: Upper Hunza
itinerary.text: A boat on Attabad Lake, then the Passu Cones and the Hussaini suspension bridge for those who want to try it.

itinerary.title: Hunza → Skardu
itinerary.text: Back through Gilgit, then east on the Skardu Road, high above the Indus gorge.

itinerary.title: Deosai & Shangrila
itinerary.text: Jeeps up to the Deosai plains and Sheosar Lake, then Shangrila and Upper Kachura on the way back down.

itinerary.title: Skardu → Chilas or Naran
itinerary.text: Back down the Skardu Road and the Karakoram Highway to Chilas, or over Babusar Top to Naran when the pass is open (usually June to September).

itinerary.title: Chilas or Naran → Lahore
itinerary.text: The final stretch to the motorway, arriving in Lahore in the late evening.

faqs.question: What should I pack?
faqs.answer: Layers. Mornings and nights are cold even in summer, and Deosai can be near freezing. Bring a warm jacket, comfortable walking shoes, sunglasses, sunscreen, any personal medicines and a power bank. We send a full packing list on WhatsApp after you book.

faqs.question: Will the altitude affect me?
faqs.answer: All overnight stops are below about 2,500 m. The highest point is the Deosai plateau, around 4,000 m, which we visit for a few hours only. Most travellers feel fine; drink water and take it slowly. Tell us about any heart or breathing conditions before you book.

faqs.question: What are the roads like? What if the weather delays us?
faqs.answer: The Karakoram Highway is paved but mountainous, and landslides can close sections, especially in spring. Your driver adjusts the plan and we keep you updated on WhatsApp. If a closure adds a night, we arrange the hotel and agree the cost with you before you decide.
